published_prior_art.cite: KimKimKennedy2026 gives fixed-k causal k-means risk inference and explicitly leaves k selection open; BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies generic many-score bands, not reoptimized causal codebooks.
AndrewsSoares2010 and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2019MMI concern supplied moment systems rather than adjacent differences of optimized causal quantizer risks.
Levrard2015 gives fixed-level quantization lower-bound machinery, not a causal score-tilt lower bound for adjacent normalized risks.
CaiLow2004 and Levrard2015 provide relevant lower-bound tools but do not determine the simultaneous causal quantizer frontier.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey misses KimKimWassermanKennedy2024, Hierarchical and Density-based Causal Clustering (NeurIPS 2024), the closest additional published causal-clustering result; distinguish its non-k-means, no-margin plug-in scope from the proposed growing-k inference.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed strict extension is against only KimKimKennedy2026; under the flagship rubric this single-comparator extension caps the kernel at field until it is promoted to a generic causal-quantizer class or supplies a second named causal-clustering comparator with a strict frontier.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:adjacent-local-resolution-lower-bound and oeq:sharp-joint-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The proposed converse establishes only coordinatewise standardized-separation necessity; necessity of the full Gamma_n condition and the simultaneous sqrt(log K_n) penalty remains open.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The lower-bound headline is accepted only as a coordinatewise local-resolution converse, with the multi-coordinate frontier retained as the open-ended question.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, Remark 3.1; Section 4.1, equation (10) and Lemma 4.1; Section 4.2, Assumptions A4-A6 and Lemma 4.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Remark 3.1 says k is fixed and optimal selection is not addressed; Lemma 4.1 gives the fixed-codebook efficient influence function and Lemma 4.2 gives fixed-codebook root-n normality under the listed conditions.

The paper extends causal clustering to hierarchical and density-based methods, emphasizes that these alternatives do not require the k-means margin condition, and studies plug-in rates rather than growing-k simultaneous k-means inference.
The paper develops simultaneous confidence bands for many functional parameters using approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores and high-dimensional uniform CLTs.

The paper studies a margin-type condition for empirical optimal quantizers, derives a nonasymptotic distortion bound, and discusses dependence on quantization parameters through a minimax lower bound.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Kim, Kim, Wasserman, and Kennedy (NeurIPS 2024) to related work and state a precise non-overlap: their hierarchical/density estimators are plug-in causal-clustering methods, whereas the proposed result targets reoptimized k-means adjacent-risk inference with K_n growing.

Lift Theorem 1 above the comparator-chain floor by proving the band over a stated generic class of fixed-k causal quantizer risk scores, or by adding a second named causal-clustering comparator and a strict shared frontier against both.

Add a comparison corollary that specializes the generic growth condition to the published fixed-k causal-k-means assumptions and explicitly identifies which added uniform geometry and adjacent-variance controls are necessary for the new regime.

recommended_next_step: Revise this angle: repair the missing closest causal-clustering survey item and replace the single-comparator extension framing with a genuine comparator chain or generic-class frontier before advancing.
